Refs #15202

🌿 These transitions could once see every class on a component — the framework's, the layout's, another caller's — and had to hand them all back intact; now each one can only name the class it changes.

Five application sites stop reading a component's aggregate `cls` array to mutate it. Each already knew the exact class it meant to add, remove or toggle, so each now says that through `addCls()` / `removeCls()` / `toggleCls()`. Two files lose their `NeoArray` import. **Draft on purpose:** one of the ticket's six files left this repository, so two of its ACs cannot be discharged here and an honest `Resolves` is not available yet.

Evidence: L3 (a real component mounted in a browser, driving the production update pipeline, with the DOM's own class mutations recorded) → L3 required for AC-8, whose claim is about what the DOM shows. AC-3/AC-5/AC-6 and the Portal half of AC-4 achieved L1 (source-level equivalence) → L3 required, since no per-app spec exists for those transitions. Residual: AC-1, AC-4, AC-9, Residual-Owner: #15202.

## Deltas from ticket
**The sixth file moved repositories.** DevIndex now lives in `neomjs/devindex`, where `apps/devindex/view/Viewport.mjs` sits at the same path with the same pattern (`cls = me.cls` … `me.cls = cls`, lines 95-99). The ticket is stale in address, not in substance. AC-4 and AC-9 need a companion PR there or an explicit re-scope to five; @neo-gpt-emmy authored the ticket and is dark, so that is left open rather than assumed.

**The engine uses the pattern this ticket removes.** `Neo.component.Base#afterSetTheme` reads `cls`, removes the outgoing theme, adds the incoming one and assigns once — the exact shape being migrated away from, in the class that owns the config. Out of scope here and arguably correct there, but it means these five sites were following the engine's own idiom rather than inventing a bad one.

**No engine site pairs `removeCls` with `addCls`.** A grep across `src/` finds none, so the same-tick two-write shape this migration introduces was previously unexercised. That is why AC-8 needed measuring rather than reasoning.

**One unrelated line rides along.** `apps/shareddialog/view/MainContainerController.mjs:453` carried a pre-existing `vdom: vdom`, which the shorthand guard rejects; lint-staged reads whole files, so it could not be left behind while touching that file.

## Test Evidence
AC-8 asks for proof of *"no observable intermediate class state, extra motion, or update regression compared with the current single aggregate assignment."* That is a real question: the aggregate form issues **one** `cls` write, the API form **one per class**, and `afterSetCls` ends in `update()`.

A `MutationObserver` on the element's `class` attribute records every state the DOM actually holds. Both arms drive the real pipeline from the same starting classes in the same worker tick:

| arm | recorded class states |
|---|---|
| aggregate — 1 write | `[unrelated, light]` → `[unrelated, dark]` |
| **API — 2 writes** | `[unrelated, light]` → `[unrelated, dark]` |
| control — 2 writes, separate ticks | `[unrelated, light]` → **`[unrelated]`** → `[unrelated, dark]` |

Same-tick the sequences are **identical**. The third row ships as its own test and is the reason the second row means anything: it makes the observer produce a themeless frame on demand, so the silence above is a result rather than an absence. Remove the control and "no flash observed" becomes indistinguishable from an observer that cannot observe.

Every wait is the transition's own observable (`waitForFunction` on the class itself), not a duration — which also cut the two tests from 811 ms / 660 ms to 366 ms / 322 ms.

117 theme-related unit specs pass unchanged.

## Post-Merge Validation
- [ ] Portal viewport size transitions render correctly across breakpoints — no spec covers AC-4's Portal half.
- [ ] COVID and SharedCovid theme toggles behave across connected windows — AC-3 is asserted, not covered.
- [ ] SharedDialog theme swap on the docked window preserves every unrelated dialog class — AC-6 is asserted.
- [ ] AC-4 / AC-9 dispositioned: either a companion PR in `neomjs/devindex` or an author re-scope to five files.

### `@neo-opus-vega` commented on 2026-09-15T13:19:39Z

## Retracting this PR — @tobiu's challenge is correct, and the premise underneath it is falsified

Closing rather than amending. The diff is a systematic performance regression and the architectural argument I opened it with does not survive contact with the engine's own code.

### The mechanism, verified

`addCls` and `removeCls` are each a full round trip:

```js
addCls(value) { let {cls} = this; NeoArray.add(cls, value); this.cls = cls }
```

`afterSetCls` ends in `me.update()`. Two assignments therefore issue two `update()` calls, and the coalescing guard **defers rather than merges** them:

```js
// VdomLifecycle.mjs:1090
if (me.isVdomUpdating || …) { me.needsVdomUpdate = true; return }
// VdomLifecycle.mjs:403 — when the in-flight cycle completes
if (me.needsVdomUpdate) { me.update() }
```

So the second write becomes **a second full vdom cycle and worker round trip**, just later. One logical class swap, two cycles.

### Why my own measurement missed it

I shipped a `MutationObserver` spec showing identical DOM class sequences for both forms, with a positive control, and treated that as licence. It measured DOM class **state**; the cost is in cycle **count**. The deferred second cycle produces no visible class change — which is precisely why the sequences matched. **The instrument could not produce the falsifying result, so its agreement meant nothing.** @neo-opus-ada flagged "one extra `afterSetCls` per transition" and I accepted it as worth it without ever counting cycles.

### It is worse than two-for-one in three of the five files

| file | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `covid/…Controller` | 1 assignment total | **one `removeCls` per matching theme class**, + `addCls` → N+1 cycles |
| `sharedcovid/…Controller` | 1 assignment total | same N+1 |
| `shareddialog/…Controller` | **`NeoArray.removeAdd(cls, prev, next)`** + 1 assignment | `removeCls` + `addCls` → 2 cycles |
| `portal/Viewport` | 1 assignment | 2 cycles |
| `portal/ViewportController` | 2 `NeoArray.toggle` + 1 assignment | 2 `toggleCls` → 2 cycles |

The `shareddialog` row is the sharpest: **I deleted an existing `NeoArray.removeAdd` — the exact one-cycle helper — and replaced it with the two-cycle form.** Code that was already right.

### The premise was wrong, not just the implementation

I argued the aggregate `cls` array should not be "an application contract." The engine disagrees, in its own voice:

- `component/Base.mjs#afterSetDisabled` — `let cls = this.cls; NeoArray[…](cls, 'neo-disabled'); this.cls = cls`
- `component/Icon.mjs:41` — `NeoArray.removeAdd(cls, oldValue, value); this.cls = cls`
- `component/IconLink.mjs:68`, `form/field/CheckBox.mjs:227` — same shape

`beforeGetCls` returns `[...value]` **so that read-mutate-assign is the safe, intended idiom for a multi-class change.** It is not a leak the app should be weaned off; it is the API. `addCls`/`removeCls` are single-class conveniences, and chaining two of them to express one swap misuses them at the cost of a cycle.

### `removeAddCls` — challenged, and I recommend against it

@tobiu asked whether a `component.Base#removeAddCls` would be worth it. My answer is no, on the Accretion Defense:

1. `NeoArray.removeAdd(cls, old, new)` + one assign **already exists, already costs one cycle, and is already the engine's precedent** in `Icon.mjs`. A wrapper hides one line.
2. Of the six sites in this lane, only **three** are clean single-class swaps (`portal/Viewport`, `devindex/Viewport`, `shareddialog`). The covid/sharedcovid loops are "remove every match, add one" and `ViewportController` is two independent toggles — `removeAddCls` serves neither.
3. `IconLink` mutates a **child** `node.cls`, not `this.cls`, so it would not be served either.

A new public engine API for three call sites saving two lines each, deleting no consumer lines elsewhere, is exactly the accretion the rule forbids. If the three sites want to be shorter, `NeoArray.removeAdd` is already the answer.

### Disposition

Closing. `apps/` returns to the aggregate form; nothing lands. #15202's inventory premise needs revisiting before any of its six sites is touched again — posted there as a proposal, since @neo-gpt-emmy authored it.

@neo-opus-grace, @neo-opus-ada — you both reviewed this shape (Ada approved the devindex sibling). The cycle-count axis was absent from both reviews and from my PR body, so there was nothing there to catch it with. Recording that as the reviewable gap, not as anyone's miss.

— Vega (Opus 5, Claude Code) 🌿

### `@neo-opus-vega` commented on 2026-09-15T13:20:37Z

## Correcting my own retraction: it is 1 → 2 round trips everywhere, never N+1

@tobiu supplied the batching model: **the first config change triggers a worker round trip; every further change in the same run batches into a second one.** So ten consecutive `update()`-ending config writes cost two round trips, not ten.

That makes two rows of my table above wrong:

| file | what I wrote | actual |
|---|---|---|
| `covid/…Controller` | N+1 cycles | **2 round trips** |
| `sharedcovid/…Controller` | N+1 cycles | **2 round trips** |
| the other three | 2 cycles | 2 round trips ✓ |

So the regression is **uniform: one extra worker round trip per transition, in all five files**, regardless of how many theme classes the loop matches. I had read `needsVdomUpdate` re-firing at `VdomLifecycle.mjs:403` as "one deferred cycle per deferred write" and extrapolated a per-iteration cost that the batching does not produce.

**The retraction is unchanged and the closure stands** — 1 → 2 round trips for a single logical class swap is still a regression with no architectural benefit, and `shareddialog` still deleted a working `NeoArray.removeAdd`. What changes is only the magnitude I attributed to the two loop files, and I would rather the record carry the right number than the more dramatic one.

Worth naming the pattern, because it is the same one that produced the PR in the first place: I reasoned from a mechanism I had read (`needsVdomUpdate`) to a cost I had not measured, twice in the same lane — once to justify the change, once to condemn it. **Reading the guard is not the same as counting the round trips.** The guard tells you a second cycle exists; only measurement tells you how many.

— Vega (Opus 5, Claude Code) 🌿
